title: Road Hazard Certificate Refunds on a Promotional Ticket: Crestline Credit Card Deferred Interest
content:
A refund Crestline paid back to the Crestline Credit Card for a road hazard certificate (Road Hazard Protection) sold on a deferred-interest plan's ticket reaches the card without the ticket number, so it is matched to the plan through the certificate record and taken off the plan's balance left; because an accrual already recorded is never reversed for a credit, its interest effect depends on when it was paid: when it was paid on or before the closing date of the plan's last recorded accrual, interest on it at the daily rate for each stub day is taken off; when it was paid after that closing date, interest on it for each day from its payment date through the last day of the period, both days counted, is taken off; otherwise nothing is taken off. The interest taken off reduces the deferred interest assessed.

## Matching the refund

- **The certificate:** the Road Hazard Protection certificate whose purchase ticket number is the plan's ticket number and whose tender was the Crestline card.
- **The refund:** that certificate's cancellation refund, paid to the Crestline card, with its amount and date.

- **Recorded balance:** the plan's purchase amount less the payment allocations recorded for it and less the merchandise credits that carry its ticket number.
- **Daily rate:** the account's purchase rate divided by 365 (the product's daily rate basis in days).
- **Stub days:** the days from the day after the closing date of the plan's last recorded accrual through the last day of its period (its expiration date).

## Decision table

| Refund paid to the card | Interest taken off |
|---|---|
| on or before the last accrual's closing date | refund multiplied by the daily rate, multiplied by the stub days |
| after that closing date, up to the last day of the period | refund multiplied by the daily rate, multiplied by the days from the payment date through the last day of the period, both counted |
| no such refund, or paid after the period ended | nothing |

## Cases (hypothetical)

Hypothetical figures use a purchase rate of 36.5 percent, so that the daily rate is a round 0.1 percent.

- A 90.00 USD certificate refund paid 2 June, last accrual closing 10 June, period's last day 14 June: 4 stub days; 0.36 USD is taken off.
- The same refund paid 12 June: 12 to 14 June, 3 days; 0.27 USD is taken off.
